newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-ZAIREAN CLUBS FACE DISADVANTAGE IN CUP COMPETITIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAIREAN CLUBS FACE DISADVANTAGE IN CUP COMPETITIONS.

text.p: Zairean clubs intend to keep up a spirited challenge for two of Africa's continental club competitions despite being barred from playing at home in this weekend's second round, first leg matches.

Dragons of Kinshasa and the provincial club AS Bantous have been told by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) that they will play single elimination matches at the home venue of their respective opponents in the African Cup Winners' Cup and the CAF Cup because of the ongoing civil war in Zaire.

Dragons play in the Ivory Coast this weekend against local military club SO Armee in their Cup Winners' Cup tie while AS Bantous will travel to Uganda in two weeks to face Kampala City Council in the CAF Cup.
"It is a big disappointment for our teams and certainly a big disadvantage," said Zairean Football Association secretary-general Biangany Gomanu.
Dragons, who are based in Kinshasa, have not been affected by the civil war but AS Bantous are based in Mbuji Mayi, the diamond-producing centre which has fallen to the rebel army of Laurent Kabila.
Gomanu insisted that Bantous would still be able to honour their fixture. "They have three players who have been with our national team and the others will fly out via Kenya and join up with them."
Zaire's national team have also been forced to play their last two World Cup qualifying matches at neutral venues because of the war.

Neither of the Zairean sides count among the favourites in this year's competitions. In the Cup Winners' Cup, holders Arab Contractors of Egypt, Tunisia's Etoile Sahel and Morocco's Royal Armed Forces look to have trophy-winning credentials.
Contractors, who beat Zairean club Sodigraf in last year's final, travel to Zambia to play Nchanga Rangers while Etoile Sahel have a particularly difficult away game against Ghana's Hearts of Oak.
The Moroccan army team also travel for the first leg against FC 105 of Libreville, Gabon.
Tunisia's Esperance head the field of contenders in the CAF Cup and go to Burkina Faso to play USFA in Ouagadougou on Sunday.

The African Champions' Cup also sees second round, first leg action at the weekend with holders Zamalek of Egypt home to Mufulira Wanderers of Zambia and 1995 winners Orlando Pirates of South Africa travelling across the border to play in Harare against Zimbabwean champions Caps United.
Sixteen clubs left in the competition are chasing places in the new African Champions' League, which will be launched in August once the field is cut down to eight.
The competition carries prize money for the first time with teams earning $150,000 just for qualifying and standing to make more for every point they earn.
The second round, second leg games in all three competitions will be played on the weekend of May 16-18.
